statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 18% while the premarket retracement is functioning, with Stress elevated at 54% on the oil, long-yield and AI-repricing backdrop.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON and Tail remains below the block threshold. A narrow elevated-risk window is published from 13:30Z to 15:30Z, spanning the US cash open, the opening auction and the Michigan preliminary release. headline: Nasdaq-100 premarket bounce holds Thursday's support shelf; Tail low into the US cash open
body: NQ December futures trade near 31,205 (+0.76%, premarket range 30,953-31,266) after the Nasdaq-100 cash index fell 1.39% to 30,725.81 on Thursday, its worst session in roughly seven weeks. Thursday's decline followed a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was approximately $50bn at end-September, about $20bn below figures previously circulated to investors; the gap is largely an accounting difference over whether cloud-partner revenue is counted rather than lost sales. A subsequent Bloomberg report that OpenAI still expects to reach or exceed $70bn annualised by year-end has steadied the AI complex, and semiconductors that led Thursday's 3.4% gauge decline are bid in premarket trade. Thursday's 30,987-30,838 support shelf held on test, VIX has eased to 15.2 with no volatility expansion, WTI is down roughly 0.8% near $90.6 after Thursday's 3.6% surge, and the 10-year Treasury yield has slipped about 5bp to 5.23%. That combination describes a functioning retracement rather than a failing one, which is why Tail stays in the low band. The stress backdrop is nonetheless genuinely difficult: long-dated yields sit near 24-year highs, Brent near $102-104 reflects an active Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption plus Gulf of Mexico hurricane shut-ins, and Fed commentary continues to debate further tightening. Those factors are scored as Stress and Confidence inputs, not as Tail, consistent with the contract's separation of a difficult environment from a pathological price path. The near-term checkpoints are the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, whose 1-year inflation expectations were last 4.6%; a failed open that loses 30,838 with the AI complex leading would be the first genuine evidence of a second leg. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final fifteen slots of this forecast describe a closed venue with no tradeable price path.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover Thursday's AI-led decline and the overnight recovery. Tail peaked at 28% (orange, trend-down) in the 17:00Z slot as the OpenAI revenue report drove the Nasdaq-100 down 1.39% and the semiconductor gauge down 3.4%, with Stress reaching 72%. Risk then decayed steadily through the US close and the Asian and European sessions as futures retraced higher: Tail returned to the 16-18% low band from 20:00Z onward and Stress fell from the mid-60s to 46% by 10:00Z, with the dominant mode shifting to trend-up from 07:00Z as the recovery extended. The final slot ticked Stress back to 49% as the European session approached the US open. All 24 hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment and none were reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The window splits sharply into nine live hours and fifteen closed ones. Tail rises from 18% to a 23% peak in the 14:00Z slot, covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, then decays through the US afternoon before a second, smaller 22% cluster at 20:00Z for the cash close and the Collins remarks. All live-hour values stay in the watch band or below: the published structure is a retracement that held support, and the contract requires observed persistent one-way extension or multiple aligned current amplifiers before Tail blocks. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00Z, so the remaining fifteen slots describe a closed venue where no mean-reversion failure can occur; Tail falls to 12-14% and Confidence steps down from 86% to 75% to reflect the absence of live price discovery rather than any benign structural read. Latent weekend gap risk from the Iran and Hormuz situation would express only at the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, outside this window.

forecastDetail.comment: Premarket slot. NQ Dec futures near 31,205 (+0.76%) have reclaimed Thursday's 30,987-30,838 shelf while VIX eases to 15.2, WTI slips 0.8% and the 10-year sits at 5.23%. A functioning retracement keeps Tail in the low band with the cash open still ahead.

Cash open at 13:30Z is the first live test of the bounce. Tail lifts to the watch band for checkpoint risk only; shallow pullbacks on an extending open would firm the picture, while losing 30,838 with semiconductors leading is the adverse path.

Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation expectations at 14:00Z land 30 minutes into cash trade. With 1-year expectations last 4.6% and long yields near 24-year highs, this is the session's highest conditional whipsaw risk, hence the 23% Tail peak.

Digestion hour after the open and the Michigan release. Two-way range with genuine retracements would let Tail decay; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first real evidence of a second AI-repricing leg rather than a completed one.

European cash close thins index liquidity. Contained midday ranges are the base case and pull Tail back toward the low band, though a midday trend leg holding session extremes would keep risk elevated into the afternoon.

No scheduled US release until the 20:00Z Collins remarks, so decaying intraday volatility is the base case and the mapped policy state reverts to EA_ON. Elevated oil and high long yields keep Stress in the elevated band regardless.
